metadata.title: DERELICT: Final Project Pitch
metadata.note: CSYE 7270 Assignment 8 pitch film, built by Claude Code from pitch/PROJECT-BRIEF.md. Narration speaks as the student, in the first person. Every visual is labelled: real capture, scripted capture, fixture, constructed on screen or generated. No Remotion, no walker opening, no outro card, no instructor name or handle.

skin_warnings: NO RENDERABLE BEATS: no beat carries a shot.remotion.pattern or Manim annotation — the pipeline will render NOTHING and every slot becomes a YOU-slate. The sheet was authored without the scene contract.

beats.question: title
beats.narration_text: DERELICT. I'm Sarthak Sargar, and this is my final project pitch, for a gameplay programmer or a tools programmer role.

beats.question: 1. What is it?
beats.narration_text: DERELICT is a small top-down 3D zombie shooter in four connected factory rooms, lit by a flashlight. I will take it to a finished one-run slice, from the title screen to a win or death screen, together with the test and capture toolkit that checks every layer. When it is done, it will be a Windows build in one folder, plus the repository, so you can rerun the checks yourself.

qc.contrast_reason: Full-frame game footage is dark by design (a flashlight-lit level) on a dark page; contrast is measured on the essential text regions instead of the whole frame.

beats.question: 2. Why would anyone care?
beats.narration_text: For the player, it is a short run in the dark. A burst where each bullet lands, smoke from your own wounds, a counter that turns red when ammo runs low, and a visible reload all tell you what is happening. For a reviewer, it is a small game built so that you can check how I work in a few minutes.

qc.contrast_reason: Full-frame game footage is dark by design (a flashlight-lit level) on a dark page; contrast is measured on the essential text regions instead of the whole frame.

beats.question: 2. What makes it different?
beats.narration_text: The nearest game I have played is Call of Duty's zombies mode. DERELICT is not bigger or better than that. It is single-player, top-down, four rooms, and meant to be small enough to open in a minute. The difference is that, from the shader assignment on, every layer has tests a stranger can rerun. I have also played the GTA games up to GTA 4. DERELICT does not try to be open-world.

beats.question: 3. Who opens it, and what do they do?
beats.narration_text: The reader is a lead engineer, a hiring manager or a recruiter. In the finished version, they will unzip the build, run the game, press Start, and be shooting within a minute. A tools reader will open the README and run one test command. None of that exists yet. There is no export today.

beats.question: 4. What does it prove about me?
beats.narration_text: Here is what exists today, by tag. Shaders and materials, in assignment five. Two particle effects in assignment six, with their GPU cost measured on my RTX 4050 laptop, inside a budget set in advance. Animation and state in assignment seven, with structure and edge tests. And under all of it, verification: pinned tests, and mutations that had to fail.

beats.question: 4. Evidence: a real test run
beats.narration_text: These lines are copied from a real log of the reload edge test, from assignment seven. Fire, a second reload and death are tried at every phase boundary. Ninety-eight checks pass, and none fail.

shot.visual_label: constructed on screen from real log lines

beats.question: 4. What a reviewer can and cannot conclude
beats.narration_text: So what can you conclude? That I can specify, direct, verify and measure game systems with an AI agent. Not that I hand-wrote the shaders, effects or animation. I directed Claude Code to build them, and the repository says so. And I have not yet judged the effects and the animation in play myself.

beats.question: 5. In, out, first
beats.narration_text: In scope: one run from title to end screen, a Windows export, the layers already built, my own checks in my own words, and the known issues fixed or written down. Out: multiplayer, saving, more rooms, new enemies and a web build. The first piece I will make run is the Windows export, played through to the end screen, with its checksum recorded.

beats.question: 6. What could sink it?
beats.narration_text: The risk is effects that pass their tests but don't look as designed. In assignment six, Claude Code found that in this version of Godot, billboard particles ignore the particle scale, so the impact puff never grows. These are the fixture frames. One fix was tried and reverted. I will try the next one, judge it in play, and if it still fails, ship it as a documented limit.

beats.question: 7. Why this project?
beats.narration_text: Why this project? Mostly to learn. Godot shaders, particles, animation, testing, and directing an AI agent were all new to me, and the tagged assignments are the evidence. What I already had was playing games like this one.

beats.question: Exists today versus will exist
beats.narration_text: So, today: the core loop, three props, a shader, two effects, two animations and the toolkit, each at its tag. Still to come: the export, a scripted run against it, my own checks, the effect fixes, and a README a stranger can follow.

beats.question: end card
beats.narration_text: That's DERELICT. The repository and its tag are on screen. Thanks for watching.
